stateRatePct.note: A 6.5% excise tax on the title, charged on the price certified by the dealer less any trade-in. The statute sets a $100 minimum, which the calculator does not apply.

tradeInReducesBase.note: Total purchase price is the agreed price less an allowance for trade-in. Only one trade-in can be used, and its owner must be an owner of the vehicle bought or a listed relative.

local.note: The title excise tax is a state tax and the MVA manual lists no county or city vehicle tax. Neither says outright that none applies.

sources.title: Maryland MVA - Interactive title and registration manual (PDF)

outOfStateCredit.note: The MVA applies a credit for another state's sales or excise tax only for an applicant who has been a Maryland resident for sixty days or less. The calculator assumes an existing resident, so no credit is applied.

amount.note: Yearly amounts from July 1, 2025. The law uses the manufacturer's shipping weight; the calculator uses the weight you enter. Maryland registers for two years at a time, so you pay two years of this fee when you register.

amount.note: Charged per registration year, so two years are paid with a two-year registration.

notes: Maryland registers vehicles for two years at a time; the yearly fee and surcharge are shown here.
The $100 minimum excise tax and the private sale rules for older vehicles are not applied.
Any electric vehicle surcharge, lien recording fees and dealer processing charges are not included.

content.intro: {state} charges a {stateRate} excise tax when the title is issued, on the price less any trade-in. Registration is priced by weight and paid two years at a time.

howItWorks.text: The excise tax is charged on the total purchase price, which is the agreed price less an allowance for a trade-in.
Only one trade-in can be used, and when the trade-in allowance is as large as the price, no excise tax is due.
The yearly registration fee depends on the manufacturer's shipping weight. A surcharge is added for each year.

faq.q: Does {state} credit tax I paid in another state?
faq.text: Only if you have been a {state} resident for sixty days or less, and only for state sales or excise tax, not local tax.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the excise tax in {state}?
faq.text: Yes. The tax is charged on the price less the trade-in allowance, and only one trade-in can be used per purchase.
